title: Latimer v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained in part as to specifications 1, 2, and 3, each sustained in part; specifications 4, 5, and 6 not sustained. Trial judgment voided. Because the earlier one-year definite suspension expired 5/23/12, appellant is a member of Chicago Metro Presbytery without call. No remand stated.
first_summary: The SJC sustained Rev. Stuart Latimer's appeal from Chicago Metro Presbytery's judgment deposing him for pursuing an unbiblical divorce. It held Presbytery clearly erred in finding sin in his June 27, 2012 divorce filing and voided the trial judgment; it rejected the remaining specifications. Because his prior one-year suspension had expired, he was a member of Presbytery without call.
summary: A presbytery deposed a minister for violating his seventh vow by pursuing an unbiblical divorce after he filed a civil petition. The SJC sustained the appeal in part: the presbytery clearly erred in finding sin in the filing, because the record did not conclusively show intent to divorce rather than protect his children, and the wife's counter-filing undermined the failure-to-withdraw inference. The SJC rejected prejudice, irregularity, and venue claims, voided the trial judgment, and noted that his expired prior suspension left him a presbytery member without call. Divorce precedents are fact-specific.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2013-10, Latimer v. Chicago Metro Presbytery, SJC decision dated May 14, 2014; panel draft amended and adopted by SJC vote of 18 concurring, 0 dissenting, 1 recused, 0 abstaining, 5 absent (lines 13–19, 229–233).
evidence_notes.dispute: Presbytery charged Latimer with violating his seventh ordination vow by pursuing an unbiblical divorce after his adultery confession and his wife's separation; trial found him guilty and deposed him; he appealed six specifications (lines 19, 23–29, 103–133).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Appeal sustained; specifications 1–3 sustained in part, 4–6 not sustained. SJC held Presbytery clearly erred because filing a divorce petition did not itself show sinful intent; the record lacked conclusive evidence of intent to divorce rather than protect the children, and the wife's counter-filing undercut the failure-to-withdraw inference (lines 139–145, 169–183). Specifications 4–6 were rejected for lack of record support, no shown harm, or insufficient burden (lines 185–223).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The majority cautions that the decision should not be treated as persuasive precedent because divorce outcomes are fact-specific (lines 227–229). Separate concurring opinions discuss definite versus indefinite suspension and the missing proof of 'pursuit' but are not the SJC's adopted reasoning (lines 235–341).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate incorporated decision is used; the operative reasoning is the SJC decision in this case (lines 229–231).

source_limits: Record excerpts only. The wife's 7/9/12 email or text is not in the record (line 51); Mrs. Latimer did not attend trial (line 39); the record does not show the later civil divorce outcome (lines 337–339). Concurring opinions are separate and not adopted as the decision.
